name: Lightning Roulette
how: Place bets as on a single-zero wheel — the layout and payouts are standard European roulette.
Between one and five numbers are struck by lightning and given a multiplier from 50× to 500×.
Straight-up wins on a struck number pay the multiplier instead of 35:1; all other bets pay as normal.
why: The 29:1 straight-up payout is what funds the multipliers. Outside bets keep the standard 97.30%; straight-up bets sit closer to 97.10% because six units of the 35:1 payout are taken back and returned as the 50×–500× strikes. You are trading a slightly worse average for a much longer tail.

name: Crazy Time
how: Bet on numbers 1, 2, 5 or 10, or on one of the four bonus segments.
A top slot above the wheel draws a random bet-and-multiplier pairing before each spin.
Landing a bonus segment moves you into Cash Hunt, Pachinko, Coin Flip or Crazy Time.
why: Returns differ per segment: the number bets are the highest-RTP way to play it and the bonus segments are the lowest. Most players do the opposite of what the maths says.

name: Blackjack VIP
how: Seven seats, eight decks, dealer stands on all 17s.
Double after split allowed; split up to three hands.
Play basic strategy — deviation is what turns a 0.71% edge into a 2% one.
why: The 99.29% figure assumes basic strategy and no side bets. Both side bets are materially worse than the main game — treat them as entertainment, not value.

name: Speed Baccarat A
how: Bet Player, Banker or Tie before the deal.
Cards are dealt face-up; third-card rules resolve automatically.
Banker wins are charged 5% commission.
why: Banker is the only bet worth making. The Tie bet loses over fourteen cents on the dollar in expectation and exists to move the hold.

name: Monopoly Big Baller
how: Buy up to four bingo cards before the draw.
Twenty balls are drawn; matching lines pay out.
Rolling a Chance or Big Baller ball adds multipliers or the board bonus.
why: The slowest format on the floor at roughly four minutes a round, which makes hourly loss low even though the RTP is mid-table.

name: Mega Wheel
how: Bet on one or more of the 54 wheel segments.
A Mega Multiplier of 2× to 500× is applied to a random segment before the spin.
Wins pay the segment odds, multiplied if the multiplier hit your number.
why: The closest Pragmatic gets to Crazy Time, at a tenth the entry stake. Fewer bonus layers means less variance for the same broad return.

name: Infinite Blackjack
how: Unlimited players share one dealing hand — no waiting for a seat.
Six-card Charlie rule pays automatically on six cards without busting.
No splitting; doubling is available on any two cards.
why: The highest published return of any live table we track. The trade-off is no splitting, which flattens the strategy but not the maths.

name: Dragon Tiger
how: One card to Dragon, one to Tiger. Higher card wins.
Bet Dragon, Tiger, Tie or Suited Tie.
Ties return half your stake on Dragon or Tiger bets.
why: The fastest live format on the floor. Twenty-second rounds at a 3.73% edge burn a bankroll faster than baccarat despite the similar look.

name: Auto Roulette
how: A mechanical wheel spins with no dealer, filmed live.
Standard European single-zero layout and payouts.
Rounds run continuously every 25 seconds.
why: Cleanest return of any roulette variant because nothing is skimmed for multipliers — but 144 spins an hour means the 2.70% edge is applied more often than at any dealt table.

name: Sweet Bonanza CandyLand
how: Bet on a colour segment or one of the three bonus rounds.
The wheel spins; colour wins pay fixed odds.
Bonus segments open a Sweet Bonanza-styled tumbling round with multipliers.
why: The rare game show where bonus and base returns are within two hundredths of each other, so bet preference is about pacing rather than value.

name: Football Studio
how: Two cards are dealt — Home and Away. Higher card wins.
Bet Home, Away or Draw.
Studio hosts read the round like a match broadcast.
why: Dragon Tiger in a football wrapper. Identical maths, so pick it for the presentation and avoid the Draw exactly as you would avoid the Tie.

name: Craps Live
how: Bet the Pass or Don’t Pass line before the come-out roll.
Back it with free odds once a point is set — the odds bet carries no house edge.
Avoid the centre proposition bets entirely.
why: With full odds behind the line this is the best return available in a live studio. The proposition bets in the middle of the table are the worst — a sixteen percent hold.
